epitaph: Where it all started: one team and one car.
story: MechaEagles was founded at Boston College in fall 2024 as a Baja SAE racing and engineering team, with one goal: give students the chance to build real machines.

epitaph: The year the subteams got their own tables.
story: The team organized into Science, Programmatics and Engineering divisions, with subteams for suspension, steering, roll cage, drivetrain and fabrication.
structure: Divisions that year: Science, Programmatics and Engineering.
support: Autodesk Fusion: CAD software licenses and manufacturing support
Boston College Engineering: funding and shop access
IGOS Welding: bolts and welding materials

epitaph: One car became four teams. Still being written.
story: MechaEagles became four engineering teams: Baja SAE, AeroEagles, Combat Robotics and AI Safety, with Programmatics keeping all of them running.

AeroEagles submitted its NASA Student Launch 2027 proposal and flew three rockets on its first high-power launch day. Two came back, and one didn't. The team published that alongside the wins, and changed how it verifies recovery.
achievements: Three rockets flown and two recovered on AeroEagles' first high-power launch day
Jack Tommaney earned high-power rocketry Level 1 certification
